result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection with mixed-use commercial and residential buildings. While sidewalks and traffic signals are present, the environment is characterized by wide, unmarked asphalt areas and faded or missing crosswalk markings on the primary crossing.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crosswalk
hazards.description: The primary crossing across the side street lacks visible paint, failing to designate a safe path for pedestrians or alert drivers to their presence.

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: The roadway surface is cracked and uneven, which can create tripping hazards for pedestrians and unpredictable vehicle movements.

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The transition from the sidewalk to the street lacks ADA-compliant ramps, creating barriers for people with mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the sidewalk on the left and right

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install tactile warning strips and sloped curb ramps at all intersection corners.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban street with a marked zebra crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. While basic infrastructure like a traffic signal and crosswalk are present, the wide crossing distance and lack of a pedestrian refuge island or curb extensions increase exposure to vehicle traffic.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic and a wide painted buffer without a physical refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground, across the main roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Protection
hazards.description: The wide painted median area does not provide physical protection from vehicles for pedestrians mid-crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway, yellow painted buffer zone

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised concrete island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Pedestrian Signals
interventions.description: Ensure countdown pedestrian signals are installed and visible to provide clear timing for crossing.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban intersection with marked crosswalks and basic traffic signals in a mixed-use residential and commercial area. While sidewalks and crossings are present, the wide roadway and lack of pedestrian refuge or curb extensions increase exposure risk.

hazards.description: The wide intersection requires pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners may obscure sight lines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sight lines.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.
